testcases.Setup: Single applicant, New IBR plan, AGI in top income bracket (e.g. $180k+)
testcases.Steps: 1. Log in 2. Confirm repayment plan = New IBR on profile 3. View Overview forgiveness timeline and monthly payment
testcases.Expected Result: Forgiveness horizon shows ~240 months AND monthly IDR payment reflects the higher-income 10% discretionary-income formula (not capped at $0/low estimate)
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 1. Basic Scenarios — 'Standard IBR - Higher Income' not explicitly paired with plan+income together
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Setup: Single applicant, SAVE/REPAYE (RAP) plan, AGI near/below 150% of poverty guideline
testcases.Steps: 1. Log in 2. Confirm plan = SAVE/REPAYE on profile 3. View Overview
testcases.Expected Result: Forgiveness horizon shows ~360 months AND IDR payment is $0 or minimal, consistent with low-income formula for this plan
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 1. Basic Scenarios — 'SAVE/REPAYE - Low Income' not explicitly paired with plan+income together
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Setup: User with loans, What-If Scenarios accessible
testcases.Steps: 1. Go to What-If Scenarios 2. Set rate of return to an extreme high value (e.g. 20-30%) 3. Observe tax bomb / savings goal outputs
testcases.Expected Result: Calculator produces a bounded, non-crashing result; unrealistic inputs are either capped or flagged, not silently accepted as if reasonable
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 2. Edge Cases — 'Very High/Low Rate of Return' has no existing case
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Setup: User with loans, What-If Scenarios accessible
testcases.Steps: 1. Go to What-If Scenarios 2. Set rate of return to 0% or a negative value if the field allows it 3. Observe outputs
testcases.Expected Result: Savings goal recalculates to a conservative (higher) figure; no NaN, no crash; negative rate is either rejected or clamped to 0%
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 2. Edge Cases — 'Very High/Low Rate of Return' has no existing case
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Setup: Married user filing separately; log in specifically as the SPOUSE record (or toggle to Spouse view)
testcases.Steps: 1. Log in / toggle to Spouse Loans view 2. Confirm filing status = separately 3. Review spouse's payment and tax bomb figures
testcases.Expected Result: Spouse's own AGI (not applicant's, not combined) drives spouse's IDR payment and tax bomb; figures differ correctly from the applicant's view in P-03
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 3. Spouse Scenarios — 'Married Filing Separately - Spouse' should be an isolated check distinct from the applicant-side case (P-03)
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Setup: Married filing jointly, both have loans, 3+ children (household size 5+)
testcases.Steps: 1. Log in 2. Confirm household size on profile 3. View Overview payment estimate for both applicant and spouse views
testcases.Expected Result: Poverty guideline / discretionary income calculation reflects the larger household size consistently in both applicant and spouse views
testcases.Source / Rationale: Guide 3. Spouse Scenarios — 'Married with Children' only tested at household size 3 (P-02); larger family + spouse combination untested
testcases.TEST DATA: REFER TO PERSONA

testcases.Steps: 1. Set AGI $60k, household size 1, New IBR plan
testcases.Expected Result: Tax bomb should be approximately: (Remaining Balance after 20 years √ó 22%) in year 241. Display should show: ~$X amount as tax liability estimate.
testcases.Source / Rationale: Tax bomb calculations are core value proposition. Incorrect calculations could mislead users about financial planning. Test ensures formula matches federal tax treatment.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should prominently display tax bomb calculation and show the formula/methodology
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Single user; $150k loans; New IBR; 22% tax rate; $0 current savings

testcases.Setup: Tax Bomb - Joint vs Separate Filing
testcases.Steps: 1. Set up applicant: AGI $60k, spouse: AGI $70k, both New IBR
testcases.Expected Result: Separate filing: Each spouse's tax bomb calculated independently using their own AGI
testcases.Source / Rationale: Filing status significantly impacts AGI used in calculations. Different tax brackets could apply. Users need to understand impact of filing status on total tax liability.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design must clearly distinguish between filing separately vs jointly and show impact on both spouses' calculations
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Married couple both with $150k loans, filing separately

testcases.Steps: 1. Test each household size: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8+
testcases.Expected Result: For AGI at/below 150% poverty guideline: Monthly payment = $0 or near-zero
testcases.Source / Rationale: Discretionary income calculation depends entirely on poverty guidelines. Incorrect thresholds lead to wrong payment estimates. Federal guidelines change annually.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show poverty guideline used and how it affects payment calculation. Should provide reference to current HHS guidelines
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Single user, varying AGI; household sizes 1-8

testcases.Steps: 1. Set AGI $40k, household size 1, New IBR
testcases.Expected Result: For $40k AGI: Monthly payment ‚âà $151
testcases.Source / Rationale: Payment calculations are fundamental. Users rely on these for budgeting. Small errors compound over 20-30 year repayment periods.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should display calculation breakdown: (AGI - Poverty Guideline) √ó 10% / 12. Should show annual and monthly amounts
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Single user; $100k loans; 10% AGI; various incomes

testcases.Setup: Forbearance Month Impact on Forgiveness Date
testcases.Steps: 1. Set repay_start_date: Jan 2024
testcases.Expected Result: Forbearance months must NOT count toward forgiveness period.
testcases.Source / Rationale: Forbearance tracking is critical for accurate timeline. Users need to know how forbearance affects their forgiveness date. This is a federal requirement.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should clearly show forbearance months impact on timeline. Should display: 'Forgiveness Date = XXX (due to forbearance adjustment)'
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with $150k loans; 24 forbearance months recorded

testcases.Steps: 1. Set loan balance, forgiveness date (240 months), current savings $10k
testcases.Expected Result: With $10k current savings and $50k tax bomb over 240 months remaining:
testcases.Source / Rationale: Monthly savings goal is key value prop of app. Users need accurate targets to plan finances. Formula must account for time value of money.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show: Current Savings + (Monthly Goal √ó Months Remaining) = Estimated Tax Bomb. Should show progress bar
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with $150k loans; $10k current savings; varying tax rates

testcases.Steps: 1. Add loan 1: $50k balance at 4.5% interest
testcases.Expected Result: Interest should accrue monthly based on loan balance √ó rate / 12. After 20 years, each loan grows significantly.
testcases.Source / Rationale: Users don't always understand interest accrual impact. App should educate users that forgiving larger final balances = larger tax bomb.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show: Current Balance vs Projected Balance at Forgiveness. Should break down interest accrued
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with multiple loans at different rates

testcases.Steps: 1. Mark joint account for tax bomb allocation
testcases.Expected Result: If 50/50 split: Applicant sees $25k available, Spouse sees $25k
testcases.Source / Rationale: Joint accounts with couples create ambiguity. Users need to understand how app allocates shared assets. Different allocation methods significantly impact individual goals.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design must explain joint account allocation method clearly. Should allow users to override allocation. Should show individual vs combined view
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Married couple; joint account $50k; applicant has $100k loans; spouse has $50k loans

testcases.Steps: 1. Set AGI $10k (below poverty guideline ~$14.5k)
testcases.Expected Result: Discretionary income is negative; payment = $0
testcases.Source / Rationale: Low-income users need accurate representation. Federal rules cap payments at $0 when below threshold. Error here affects most vulnerable users.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should have clear messaging for $0 payment scenarios. Should explain poverty guideline and why payment is $0
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with AGI $10k; household size 1

testcases.Steps: 1. Set AGI $150k, calculate monthly payment
testcases.Expected Result: Monthly payment > remaining balance/months-to-forgiveness
testcases.Source / Rationale: High-income users may pay off loans early. App should not mislead them about forgiveness timelines. Tax bomb only applies if loans are forgiven, not paid off.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should have clear callout: 'Loans will be paid off in X months (before forgiveness date)'. Should show no tax bomb in this scenario
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): High income user; $50k loans; $150k AGI; New IBR plan (240 months)

testcases.Steps: 1. Set household size: 8
testcases.Expected Result: For household 8, 2024 poverty guideline ‚âà $29,385; 150% ‚âà $44,078
testcases.Source / Rationale: Large families should qualify for lower payments. Poverty guideline lookup must be accurate. Calculation errors disproportionately affect larger families.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show: 'Household Size: 8 - Poverty Guideline: $44,078'. Should clearly show how household size affects payment
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Married couple with 6 children; household size 8

testcases.Steps: 1. Add multiple loans totaling $500k
testcases.Expected Result: Monthly payment same formula applies: (~$552/month)
testcases.Source / Rationale: High-debt scenarios are real for medical/law school graduates. Calculator must handle extreme but valid data. UX should present large numbers clearly.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should handle large numbers gracefully. Should provide perspective (e.g., 'This is equivalent to X years of your current income'). Should maybe recommend professional financial advice
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with $500k total loans; New IBR plan

testcases.Setup: Repayment Started Long Ago (15+ years in)
testcases.Steps: 1. Set repay_start_date: Jan 2009
testcases.Expected Result: Months paid: 180; Remaining: 60
testcases.Source / Rationale: Users far into repayment need different messaging. Savings goals should be compressed into shorter timeframe. This creates urgency and opportunity to validate calculation accuracy.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should prominently show: 'Years Until Forgiveness: 5' and emphasize the shorter timeline. Should adjust visual design (progress bar) to show imminent forgiveness
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with repay_start_date: Jan 2009 (15+ years ago); New IBR plan

testcases.Steps: 1. Set repay_start_date: Jul 2024 (current month)
testcases.Expected Result: Months paid: 0-1
testcases.Source / Rationale: Fresh-start users need encouragement and clear long-term perspective. Calculation should show full timeline to build confidence in plan. Lower monthly goals are achievable.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show encouraging message: 'You have the full 20-year timeline ahead. Start saving at your pace: $X/month'. Should provide long-term motivation
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User with repay_start_date: current month; New IBR plan; $150k loans

testcases.Steps: 1. Log in as Applicant
testcases.Expected Result: Applicant can see own loans + spouse loans (via toggle)
testcases.Source / Rationale: Sensitive financial data must be protected. Couples may have different privacy preferences. Unintended data exposure could violate privacy and trust.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show clear ownership: 'My Loans' vs 'Spouse Loans'. Should require explicit confirmation before sharing/editing spouse data
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Two married users (applicant & spouse) with linked accounts

testcases.Steps: 1. Adjust 'Rate of Return' slider from 7% to 5%
testcases.Expected Result: After save and refresh:
testcases.Source / Rationale: Users experiment with what-if scenarios to understand impacts. Lack of persistence frustrates workflow. Unsaved changes could mislead users about their actual plan.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should have clear 'Save' button and confirmation. Should show: 'Assumptions saved' confirmation. Should indicate which values are saved vs default
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User adjusts sliders: Rate of Return 7% ‚Üí 5%; Tax Rate 22% ‚Üí 24%

testcases.Steps: 1. Set AGI: -$500,000 (negative)
testcases.Expected Result: Negative AGI: Rejected with message 'AGI cannot be negative'
testcases.Source / Rationale: Input validation prevents garbage-in scenarios. Users may make typos or test system behavior. App must gracefully handle invalid inputs without crashing.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show inline validation messages: 'Please enter a value between $0 and $X'. Should prevent form submission if invalid
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User enters extreme values: AGI -$500k, Loan Balance $99.9M, Household Size 999

testcases.Steps: 1. Set Applicant: PSLF, Non-profit employer (assumed qualified)
testcases.Expected Result: Both spouses show:
testcases.Source / Rationale: PSLF has specific employment and eligibility requirements. Users may not actually qualify. App should not assume PSLF without verification. Must educate users on requirements.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show PSLF disclaimer prominently. Should recommend: 'Verify eligibility at studentaid.gov/pslf'. Should link to employer verification process
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User marked as PSLF; employed at non-profit; both spouses PSLF

testcases.Steps: 1. Set Applicant: PSLF (tax bomb = $0)
testcases.Expected Result: Applicant view: 'No Tax Bomb' (PSLF) - green callout
testcases.Source / Rationale: Couples with different repayment strategies need clear visibility into individual situations. Spouse toggle should make scenarios distinct and non-confusing.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should use different visual styles for PSLF vs. non-PSLF scenarios. Should provide side-by-side comparison if possible
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Applicant: PSLF; Spouse: New IBR

testcases.Steps: 1. On Overview tab, expand 'Tax Bomb Progress' accordion
testcases.Expected Result: After refresh:
testcases.Source / Rationale: Users appreciate persistent UI state. Accordion persistence improves UX by maintaining their preferred view. Must validate localStorage implementation.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should include subtle visual indicator that state is being saved (e.g., 'Your view was saved'). Should not clutter interface
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): User expands 'Tax Bomb Progress' and 'Monthly Savings Goal' accordions

testcases.Steps: 1. Resize browser to mobile width (375px iPhone)
testcases.Expected Result: On mobile:
testcases.Source / Rationale: Mobile users (likely checking on phone) need to understand spouse data. Poor mobile UX for toggle could lead to confusion about whose data they're viewing.
testcases.TEST DATA: Design should show spouse toggle prominently on mobile. Should use icon + text label. Should test tap target size (min 44x44px per WCAG)
testcases.Test Result (Pass/Fail): Married user on mobile device; < 1024px viewport
